title: Positivity of the Gaussian distribution function
statement: Let $\Phi$ be the cumulative distribution function of the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $0<\Phi(t)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ be the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function. For every real $t$, one has $0<\Phi(t)$.
